summary: Prescott NF set up a full-time lookout at the Derby Mine in 1911; the mine area later became the Highland Pines subdivision, and no source describes the lookout's remains.

facts.status_note: Forest Fire Lookout Association lists the type as unknown and the status as Abandoned; no source describes what stands at the site

events.note: Prescott National Forest set up a 'constant' (full-time) lookout at the Derby Mine location; one of two full-time lookouts on the forest, the other at Mount Union
Around 1960 the area was classified as a real estate development called Highland Pines, with over 57 homes built; the mine shaft served as its water source

notes_for_editor: The only lookout-specific source is the one 1911 sentence on the Forest Lookouts page, which does not describe the tower. The full sentence there also names the other full-time lookout as at Mt. Union; that is the Forest Lookouts page's wording and is not checked against any other source. The lookout is taken to stand at the mine because the page is named for the mine and the FFLA entry sits west of Prescott, as the mine does; check if a better source turns up. Mount Union Lookout (NHLR, built 1933) is a different tower and is not used. Peakbagging.com's Arizona table has no Derby Mine row. The Highland Pines company page (highlandpinesarizona.com) describes the subdivision's land as the old mining claims; not used. Access to the site is not stated in any source. No photos added.
